Definition: Percentage of total electricity generation from renewable sources (hydro, solar, wind, geothermal, biomass). Indicates energy sustainability and potential for distributed power solutions relevant to ICT infrastructure in off-grid areas.
revision_notes: Original score (1 = <10%) rested solely on a 2016 Worldometer figure of 4.76% hydro. World Bank WDI (EG.ELC.RNEW.ZS, checked via indexmundi mirror) and an Ember/EIA-derived tracker (chartingtheglobe.com) both record renewable electricity generation share for Comoros at 0% across all years to 2021-2023, contradicting the Worldometer figure for the same period. Cross-checked against more recent generation-capacity data (statbase.org, pvknowhow.com Comoros solar report, Africa Energy Portal): a World Bank-funded solar programme (Comoros Solar Energy Access Project) brought roughly 3-4 MW of solar PV online by 2024 plus a small (~1 MW) hydropower plant, against a diesel-dominated national fleet of around 29 MW (about 88% of installed capacity). Because thermal plants run at far higher capacity factors than solar, actual generation share is very likely still below 10%, so the categorical score of 1 (<10%) is confirmed. The comment is corrected to reflect this evidence rather than the isolated 4.76% hydro figure.
revised_comments: Renewable sources contribute a small share of Comoros's electricity generation. World Bank data record renewable electricity output at effectively 0% of total generation across the most recent reported years, reflecting the national grid's historical reliance on imported diesel. Since 2023, the World Bank-funded Comoros Solar Energy Access Project has brought roughly 3-4 MW of solar photovoltaic capacity online across the three islands, alongside a small (around 1 MW) hydropower installation, against a generation fleet still dominated by diesel thermal plants (around 29 MW, roughly 88% of installed capacity). Renewable capacity therefore remains below 10% of the generation mix, with a further approximately 9 MW of solar under construction and additional projects planned as the government pursues a target of 100% renewable energy by 2030.
